title: quercus infectoria var. syriaca
intro: Quercus infectoria var. syriaca, commonly known as Syrian Oak Gall or Gall Oak, is a plant species that belongs to the family Fagaceae. It is traditionally used in medicine and has been found to possess several health benefits, including anti-inflammatory, antibacterial, and antioxidant properties, which contribute to its therapeutic actions in treating various ailments such as fever, respiratory issues, and digestive problems. The bioactive constituents of Quercus infectoria var. syriaca include tannins, flavonoids, and phenolic acids, which are responsible for its medicinal properties. The plant's therapeutic actions can be attributed to its ability to modulate the immune system, reduce inflammation, and exhibit antimicrobial activity, making it a valuable resource in traditional medicine.
